purpose: Answers the two D-5 questions left to DevOps: how the public console-demo client obtains a WS-only demo token from self-managed Keycloak, and how svc-console-ws is disposed of without a bypass. Proposal only; D-5 remains OPEN.

Q1_issuance.answer: console-demo (public, PKCE) performs a second authorize with prompt=none and scope=ws.observe; a scope-gated Audience mapper on the optional ws-observe client scope yields aud=WS API and no other audience; lifetime <=900 s, no refresh for that token; $connect requires issuer/signature/expiry, WS audience, ws.observe, azp=console-demo, sub=demo subject and exact Origin.
Q1_issuance.client: console-demo (public, authorization code + PKCE S256, exact HTTPS redirect)
Q1_issuance.flow: second authorization request with prompt=none, top-level redirect, no iframe; interactive fallback on login_required
Q1_issuance.audience: WS API resource only (optional client scope audience mapper)
Q1_issuance.separate_or_narrowed: separate token from the same client and subject, with disjoint audience/scope from the console token
Q1_issuance.lifetime: <=900 s, no refresh token for the WS token, re-authorize instead
authorizer_checks: subprotocol contains fixed protocol id + JWT
signature via issuer JWKS, RSA alg allowlist, known kid
echo fixed protocol id only, never the token

Q2_svc_console_ws.answer: Retired: no consumer remains, and even a recreated/renamed confidential client is rejected because $connect allowlists azp=console-demo and sub=demo subject — audience/scope alone would not have prevented the bypass.
Q2_svc_console_ws.disposition: retire (delete client, credential, registry row, configuration variables)
bypass_prevention_layers: client deleted: no assertion key exists
sub == demo subject (client_credentials carries a service-account subject)
audience/scope checks are necessary but not sufficient, and are not relied on alone
Q2_svc_console_ws.callback_separation: notifier uses IAM SigV4 execute-api:ManageConnections scoped to this API/stage; no Keycloak client, no OAuth token, no browser token; CI asserts only the notifier role holds that permission

added_keycloak: optional client scope console-api (console audience, console.demo)
optional client scope ws-observe (WS audience, ws.observe)
table_changes: connection record: replace serviceBinding with azp + tokenClass=demo-ws; keep epoch/sub/environment/registryVersion/tokenExpiry/leaseExpiry
logging: exclude Sec-WebSocket-Protocol and Authorization from all log formats; CI assertion
iam: confirm only the notifier role holds execute-api:ManageConnections on this API/stage

security_conditions.registry_revocation: connection record + per-frame + idle scheduler re-read; REVOKED closes <=1 heartbeat; failed read fails closed; no refresh on the WS token
security_conditions.subprotocol_log_hygiene: log format exclusion + CI assertion; fallback = 30 s single-use ticket minted by the console API (authenticated endpoint, not a relay)
security_conditions.exact_origin: authorizer equality; forged Origin by non-browser clients is acknowledged, so Origin is context protection, not authentication
security_conditions.rate_limits: <=6 connect attempts/min/subject plus pre-auth IP/concurrency; token endpoint and prompt=none under the same WAF rule

unverified: pinned Keycloak release applies optional-scope audience mapper only when requested
prompt=none with PKCE behaves silently with a live SSO session and returns login_required otherwise
azp and demo sub are present on the second-authorize token
API Gateway WS $connect authorizer receives Sec-WebSocket-Protocol for the selected API type
JWT grammar/length limits in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol on the deployed stack
log-field exclusion is configurable on CloudFront/API Gateway/WAF as claimed
